title: "MGT 816 — The Private Firm CFO"
---

## Accounting and Finance Strategies

This course is about the CFO role at a private, entrepreneurial company. We cover accounting-based financial metrics, financial reporting, and managerial accounting, and we build the accounting system the way a company does: from the start-up phase through to exit.

The sessions run in that order: financial infrastructure, capitalization, equity compensation, forecasting, board reporting, revenue recognition, fundraising, and exits. You do two cases and two problem sets.

### What you will take from the course

Public-company finance is well covered elsewhere in the curriculum. The private firm is different: there is no market price, no analyst following, and little mandated disclosure, and the owners — founders, employees, and funds — hold claims with different rights and different incentives. The CFO sits where those claims meet.

By the end of the term you will have built these working documents yourself:

- a capitalization table from formation through a priced Series A
- a driver-based operating forecast, built with AI tools doing the analyst work and you certifying every number
- a board memo on equity compensation and its tax consequences
- a critique of a board reporting package
